title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 29
paragraphs: So he spoke, and Xerxes, pleased by what he said, answered: “Lydian host, ever since I set out from the Persian land I have met no man up to this point who wished to entertain my army, or who came before me and of his own free will offered to contribute money for the war, except you alone. You not only entertained my army magnificently but now also offer me great sums of money. To you, therefore, I give these rewards in return: I make you my guest-friend, and I will complete for you the four million staters out of my own purse by adding the seven thousand, so that your four million may not fall short by seven thousand, but you may have a round sum by my contribution. Keep what you have made for yourself, and continue always to act in this manner, for if you do, you will never have cause for regret, either now or afterwards.”
